Rashi on Pesachim 34b:10:1.hebrew: בענבים של תרומה - והאי "הקדישן" — קדושת תרומה קאמר, דבתרומה לא שייכא קדושת כלי, לא ביין ולא בענבים:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:10:1.english: With grapes of teruma - And this [phrase,] “he consecrated them,” means the consecration of teruma; for regarding teruma, the consecration of a vessel does not apply, neither to wine nor to grapes.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:10:2.english: However, those - The water of the Festival [for the libation].

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:11:1.hebrew: דרכן ואפילו טובא - לעיל קמהדר: אמרת דרכן ואחר כך הקדישן טהורות, ואפילו טובא בבת אחת?! בתמיה. והא אמרת לעיל: פחות פחות מכביצה! דאי יותר — הא איטמו משקין בכביצה מיציאת טיפה ראשונה, טומאת האוכל, שהרי יש בה כשיעור:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:11:1.english: [If] he trod on them — and even many?! - [The Gemara] is referring back to [the statement] above: You said, "[If] he trod on them and afterward consecrated them, [the liquids] are ritually pure" — and [does this mean] even many at one time?! [This is asked] in astonishment. But didn't you say above: "Less than an egg-bulk at a time"? For if [it is] more, behold, the liquids become ritually impure through an egg-bulk [of grapes] from the emergence of the first drop, [with] the ritual impurity of food, for there is the [requisite] measure in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:12:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן אי בעית אימא הכא נמי בפחות מכביצה ואי בעית אימא התם דבעינן פחות מכביצה שנגעו ענבים בראשון - כגון טמא שרץ או טמא נבילה, וכל שכן טמא מת; דכיון דהוו ענבים שני, טימאו את המשקין בכביצה משיצאת טיפה ראשונה, ואף על פי שהן חולין — דכל הפוסל את התרומה מטמא משקין להיות תחלה. "ושני עושה שלישי בתרומה" — לא גרסינן, דהא בחולין עסקינן; דאי בתרומה — הא אמרן דעבוד מעלה שמטמאה משקה עם האוכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:12:1.english: This is the reading: "If you wish, say: Here too, [it is] with less than an egg-bulk; and if you wish, say: There, where we require less than an egg-bulk, [it is a case] where the grapes came into contact with a first-[degree source of impurity]" - For example, [an item] defiled by a creeping animal or [an item] defiled by a carcass, and all the more so [an item] defiled by a corpse; for since the grapes became [an item with] second-degree [impurity], they defiled the liquids with an egg-bulk [of grapes], from [the moment] the first drop emerged. And even though they are non-sacred [produce], for anything that disqualifies terumah defiles liquids to become [an item with] first-degree [impurity]. And we do not read: "and a second-degree [source of impurity] makes a third-degree [source of impurity] in terumah," for we are dealing with non-sacred [produce]; for if [it were dealing] with terumah, haven't we said that [the Sages] enacted a stringency, that [the food] defiles the liquid along with the food?

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:12:2.hebrew: הכא דנגעו - ענבים בשני, דהוו להו שלישי. ענבים שנעשו על טהרת תרומה, משכחת בהו שלישי. הלכך, דרכן ואחר כך הקדישן — שקרא להן שם תרומה — טהורין, ואפילו דרך הרבה יחד, שהאוכל שלישי לא עשה למשקה כלום, ומתחלה לא נטמאו עם האוכל, דקודם קריאת שם לא עבוד מעלה. הקדישן לתרומה ואח"כ דרכן — טמאין, דמקריאת שם חלה המעלה עליהן, ונעשה המשקין כאוכל, הכל אחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:12:2.english: Here, where they came into contact - The grapes [came into contact] with [an item having] second-degree [impurity], so that they became [impure with] third-degree [impurity]. [With regard to] grapes that were handled according to the purity [standards] of teruma, one can find in them [a status of] third-degree [impurity]. Therefore, [if] he trod them and afterward consecrated them — that is, he designated them with the name of teruma — [the liquids] are pure, even if he trod many [grapes] together; for food [having] third-degree [impurity] does not affect liquid at all, and initially [the liquids inside] did not become impure along with the food, because prior to the designation of the name [the Sages] did not impose a higher standard. [If] he consecrated them for teruma and afterward trod them, [the liquids] are impure, because from [the time of] the designation of the name the higher standard took effect upon them, and the liquids are treated like the food, all as one.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:13:1.hebrew: אף אנן נמי תנינא - דעבוד רבנן מעלה בקדשים, ואפילו בקדושת פה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:13:1.english: We, too, have learned - That the Sages established a higher standard for consecrated items, and even for consecration through speech.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:13:2.hebrew: שתהא חיותן בכלי - באותו כלי עצמו שהוא מקדש בו מי חטאת באפרן, צריך למלאותו מן המעין, ולא ימלאם בכלי אחר ויערם לתוך זה. וכתב "ונתן", דמשמע תלושין — דמותר למלאותו בכלי אחר ויערם לתוך זה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:13:2.english: That their living state should be in the vessel - Into that very vessel in which he sanctifies the purification water with their ash, he must fill it [directly] from the spring, and he may not fill them into another vessel and pour them into this [one]. And [the Torah] wrote, "and he shall put," which implies [water that is] detached — that it is permitted to fill it into another vessel and pour them into this [one].

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:1.hebrew: כל שפסולו בגופו - פסול ודאי ובבשר עצמו — ישרף מיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:1.english: Any [offering] whose disqualification is in its body - [Where there is] a definite disqualification and [it is] in the meat itself — it shall be burned immediately.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:2.english: In the blood - For example, [if] the blood was spilled.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:3.hebrew: ובבעלים - כגון נטמאו בעלים, והפסח קיים ואין כאן מי שיאכלנו. ודם — אע"פ שפסול גמור הוא, אפילו הכי, הואיל ואינו כבשר עצמו, בעי עיבור צורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:3.english: And in the owners - For example, where the owners became impure and the Pesach [offering] is intact, and there is no one here who can eat it. And [disqualification in] the blood — even though it is an absolute disqualification, nevertheless, since it is not like [a disqualification in] the meat itself, it requires decay of form.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:4.hebrew: תנא דבי רבה בר אבוה - עיקר מילתא לא ידענא היכא, וטעמא דמילתיה בכיצד צולין:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:4.english: The tanna of the school of Rabba bar Avuh - The primary source of the matter, I do not know where [it is]; and the reason for his statement [is explained] in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:5.hebrew: אפילו פיגול - שפסול הגוף הוא, טעון עיבור צורה. והכא לא מצי לשנויי כדמשני לקמיה: מאי פסולי חטאת העוף? שנפסלו בטבול יום — דהיינו טומאה, וצורה למה לי:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:1:5.english: Even piggul - Which is a disqualification of the body, [yet it] requires decay of form. And here, he could not answer as he answers below: What are [the] disqualified bird sin-offerings? Those that were disqualified by a tevul yom — for that is [actual] ritual impurity, and why would it need [decay of] form?

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:2:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר יזרוק - את הדם. ר' אליעזר לטעמיה, דאמר בכיצד צולין: דם — אף על פי שאין בשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:2:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He sprinkles - [He sprinkles] the blood. Rabbi Eliezer follows his [own] reasoning, as he said in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin: [One sprinkles the] blood even though there is no meat.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:2:2.hebrew: רבי יהושע אומר לא יזרוק - ר' יהושע לטעמיה, דאמר: "אם אין בשר, אין דם". ו"יצא חוץ לקלעים" — בבשר קדשי הקדשים קאמר, שמחיצה שלהן חומת עזרה, כדכתיב בכולהו: "בחצר אהל מועד יאכלוה"; ואם יצאת — נפסלת, כדילפינן בכיצד צולין מ"אל הקודש פנימה":
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:2:2.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He does not sprinkle - Rabbi Yehoshua [follows] his [consistent] line of reasoning, as he said: "If there is no meat, there is no blood." And [as for] "it was taken out of the curtains" — it is speaking of the meat of most sacred offerings, whose partition is the wall of the Courtyard, as is written concerning all of them: "In the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it"; and if it went out, it is disqualified, as we derive in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Tzolin from: "Into the holy place within."

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:1.hebrew: מאי נפסל לאו בהיסח הדעת - בתמיה — דכיון דתנא נטמא ויצא, מאי פסול איכא תו? אי נפסל בעבודת דם — כגון במחשבת חוץ למקומו וחוץ לזמנו — לא קרי נפסל בשר, שהרי אף הדם נפסל, ובהא לא נימא ר' אליעזר יזרוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:1.english: What is [this] "became disqualified"? Is it not through a diversion of attention? - [This is asked] rhetorically: For since [the Tanna already] taught [the cases where it] became defiled and went out, what [other] disqualification is there still? If [one suggests that] it was disqualified during the service of the blood — such as through an intention [to consume it] outside its [proper] place or outside its [proper] time — [the Tanna] would not call [this] "the meat was disqualified," since the blood as well was disqualified, and in that [case] Rabbi Eliezer would not say "he shall sprinkle [the blood]."

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא - פסול חשש טומאה הוא, משום הכי מודה רבי יהושע שאם זרק הורצה: דאפילו נטמא ודאי, ואע"ג דטומאה פסול הגוף הוי — מרצה ציץ; ולכתחלה לא יזרוק, דקא סבר ריצוי ציץ בדיעבד הוא. ויוצא, אע"ג דלא מהני ליה ציץ, הורצה בדיעבד — דאע"ג דרבי יהושע בעי תרתי, דם ובשר, מיהו הואיל והבשר בעין, ופסול יוצא פסול מחמת דבר אחר הוא, חשבינן ליה פסול חסרון מחיצות, בפרק קמא דמנחות בסופו איכא למימר בדיעבד הורצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:2.english: Granted, if you say - [that this] disqualification is [due to] a concern of ritual impurity, for this reason Rabbi Yehoshua concedes that if he sprinkled [the blood], it is accepted: for even if it became definitely impure, and even though ritual impurity is an inherent disqualification, the frontplate effects acceptance; and ab initio he should not sprinkle, because he holds that the acceptance effected by the frontplate applies [only] after the fact. And [as for meat that] went out [beyond the curtains], even though the frontplate does not avail for it, it is accepted after the fact — for even though Rabbi Yehoshua requires both, blood and meat, nevertheless, since the meat is extant, and the disqualification of [meat that] went out is a disqualification on account of an external factor, we consider it a disqualification [due to] a lack of partitions; [and as established] at the end of the first chapter of Menachot, it can be said that after the fact it is accepted.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:3.hebrew: אלא אי היסח הדעת פסול הגוף הוא - וציץ נמי לא מרצי עליה, אמאי הורצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:3.english: Rather, if a diversion of attention is an inherent disqualification - And the frontplate also does not effect acceptance for it, why was it accepted?

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:4.hebrew: ה"ג: אלא אי אמרת פסול הגוף הוי, אמאי הורצה - ולא גרסינן: "פסול הגוף מי קא מרצי ציץ", דהא פסול יוצא נמי לא מרצי ציץ, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא (דף טז:): "הא אינו נושא אלא עון טומאה":
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:3:4.english: This is the correct reading: "Rather, if you say that it is an inherent disqualification, why was it accepted?" - And we do not read: "An inherent disqualification — does the frontplate atone [for it]?", for the frontplate also does not atone for the disqualification of [sacrificial meat that] went out, as we say in the first chapter (16b): "Behold, it bears only the iniquity of impurity."

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:4:1.english: Disqualified due to one who immersed himself during the day - And the reason [the Gemara explains it this way is] because of the frontplate [which atones for ritual impurity]:

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:1.hebrew: אמרה קמיה דר' ירמיה - הא דרב ששת לעיל, דאסורין מלאכול — משום היסח הדעת הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:1.english: He stated it before Rabbi Yirmeya - That [statement] of Rav Sheshet above, that [the reason] they are forbidden to be eaten is because of diversion of attention.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:2.hebrew: שמעתתא דמחשכן - כשאין יודעין טעמו של דבר, בודין מלבם טעם שאינו:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:2.english: Teachings that are dim - When they do not know the reason for a matter, they fabricate from their heart a reason that is not [so].

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:3.english: A dark place - Babylonia is low-lying.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:4.hebrew: לא שמיע לכו כו' - ומכאן יכולין ללמוד טעמה של משנה, דאסורין מלאכול — משום מעלה: דאף על גב דמהניא זריעה לחולין, עבוד רבנן מעלה דלא תהני לתרומה להעלות לה טהרה גמורה להיתר אכילה. ומיהו, מלטמא טהרו, דלהא לא עבוד מעלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:5:4.english: Have you not heard, etc. - And from here one can deduce the reason of the Mishnah that [the growths] are forbidden to be eaten — [it is] due to a special stringency: For even though sowing is effective for non-sacred produce, the Sages enacted a special stringency that it should not be effective for terumah to confer upon it complete purity to permit [its] consumption. However, from imparting impurity they became pure, for regarding this they did not enact a special stringency.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:6:1.hebrew: מי החג - כגון של ניסוך המים דשבת שבתוך החג, היו ממלאין אותן מערב שבת. וכשנטמאו, אין יכולין לילך ולמלאות מן השילוח בשבת, וטורח הוא למלאות מבור הגדול בגלגל; והלך והשיקם באמת המים שבעזרה. ומים — סלקא להו השקה, דזו היא זריעתן, משעברו עליהן מי המקוה ונעשה חיבור, ובטלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:6:1.english: The water of the festival - For example, [water] for the water libation of Shabbat that falls during the festival, which they would draw on the eve of Shabbat. And when it became impure, they could not go and draw from the Shiloach on Shabbat, and it is an exertion to draw from the Great Cistern with a pulley; and [so] he went and brought it into contact [with pure water] in the water channel in the [Temple] Courtyard. And for water, bringing [it] into contact [with a ritual bath] is effective, as this is its [equivalent of] planting — once the waters of the ritual bath have passed over it and a connection was formed, and it was nullified.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:7:1.hebrew: ואח"כ הקדישן - שעדיין לא קרא עליהן שם, או לא קידשו בכלי שרת — טהורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:7:1.english: And then consecrated them - For he had not yet designated a name upon them, or had not sanctified them in a service vessel — [they are] pure.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:7:2.hebrew: אין זריעה להקדש - לטהרו בכך, דמעלה עשו בקדשים. הכא נמי, אין זריעה לתרומה, דמעלה עשו:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:7:2.english: Planting is not [effective] for consecrated items - To purify it thereby, for they enacted a higher standard regarding consecrated items. Here too, planting is not [effective] for teruma, for they enacted a higher standard.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:8:1.english: This teaching - That of Rabbi Oshaya.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:8:2.hebrew: הקדישן בכלי שרת קאמרת - דכיון דקדושין הן קדושת הגוף, עבדינהו להו רבנן מעלה; אבל משום קדושת פה — דמלאן בכלי חול לשם חג — לא עבדי להו מעלה, ומהניא להו השקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:8:2.english: Are you saying [that he] consecrated them in a service vessel - That since they are sanctified with bodily sanctity, the Sages instituted a higher standard for them; but due to sanctity through speech — where he filled them in an unconsecrated vessel for the sake of the Festival — they did not institute a higher standard for them, and hashakah [contact with a ritual bath] is effective for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:1.hebrew: זו לא שמעתי - במעלה זו דזריעה לא שמעתי, אם בפה אם בכלי; אבל במעלה אחרת שמעתי, דאף בקדושת פה עבדוה רבנן, ואיכא למילף מינה דהוא הדין לכל מעלות שבקודש:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:1.english: I did not hear this - With regard to this higher standard of planting, I did not hear whether [it applies] through speech [or] whether in a vessel; but with regard to another higher standard, I heard that the Sages instituted it even with consecration through speech, and it can be inferred from it that the same applies to all higher standards regarding consecrated items.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:2.hebrew: דרכן ואחר כך הקדישן טהורות - לנסכים. ור' יוחנן לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל: משקין מיפקד פקידי, ולא קבילי טומאה עם האוכל. ולקמיה מפרש היכי דריך להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:2.english: If one trod on them and afterward consecrated them, they are pure - For libations. And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his [own] reasoning, as he said above: Liquids are [considered merely] deposited, and do not contract ritual impurity along with the food. And later on, [the Gemara] explains how he trod on them.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:3.hebrew: הקדישן ואח"כ דרכן טמאות - קא ס"ד, הקדיש יינו לנסכים:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:3.english: [If] he consecrated them and afterward trod on them, they are impure - [The Gemara] assumes [that] he consecrated its wine for libations.

Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:4.hebrew: טמאות - דעבוד רבנן מעלה בקדשים, דמיטמא משקה עם האוכל, ולא אמרינן בהו משקין מיפקד פקידי. והא ענבים קדושת פה הן — דאי נמי נתנן לכלי אין כלי מקדשן, דאין כלי שרת מקדשין אלא דבר הראוי לו, כדילפינן בשחיטת קדשים גבי מזבח, שנאמר: "כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש" — שומע אני בין ראוי בין שאינו ראוי? תלמוד לומר: "עולה"; וכלי שרת דומיא דמזבח נפקא לן התם:
Rashi on Pesachim 34b:9:4.english: [They are] impure - For the Sages instituted a stringency regarding consecrated items, that liquid becomes impure along with the food, and we do not say regarding them [that] liquids are [merely] deposited [inside]. And [as for the statement:] "And aren't grapes [an item of] verbal consecration?" — for even if one placed them into a [sacred] vessel, the vessel does not sanctify them, as service vessels sanctify only an item suitable for them, as we derive in [tractate] Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim] regarding the altar, as it is stated: "Whatever touches the altar shall become holy" (Exodus 29:37) — [from this] I [might] understand, whether [it is] suitable or whether [it is] not suitable? [Therefore] Scripture states: "a burnt offering" (Exodus 29:38); and [that] service vessels are comparable to the altar is derived by us there.

Tosafot on Pesachim 34b:2:1.hebrew: שאם זרק הורצה - אף על גב דאין ציץ מרצה על היוצא, רבי יהושע סבר: זריקה מועלת ליוצא, כרבי עקיבא דריש מעילה (דף ו:), דאמר: זריקה מועלת להוציא בשר מידי מעילה, וכל שכן להרצאה; דהא רבי אליעזר, דאמר הכא יזרוק, קאמר התם דלהוצאה ממעילה לא מהניא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 34b:2:1.english: "That if he sprinkled, [the offering] is accepted" - Even though the frontplate [tzitz] does not effect acceptance for [meat that was taken] outside, Rabbi Yehoshua maintains [that] sprinkling is effective for [meat that was taken] outside, in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Akiva at the beginning of Meilah (6b), who said [that] sprinkling is effective to remove meat from [the law of] sacrilege [me'ilah], and all the more so for acceptance; for Rabbi Eliezer, who says here [that] he sprinkles, says there that to remove [the meat] from sacrilege, it is not effective.

Tosafot on Pesachim 34b:7:1.hebrew: ונתן אלמא תלושין והא מחוברין נינהו - פירוש: דונתן משמע דחשיב להו תלושין, והיינו לענין קבלת טומאה, אף על פי שהן מחוברין. והשתא מייתי ראיה דאין השקה להקדש מן התורה, וכן בתרומה נמי עבוד רבנן מעלה; ופ"ה דחוק:
Tosafot on Pesachim 34b:7:1.english: “And he shall put” — apparently they are detached, but are they not attached? - Explanation: That “and he shall put” implies that it considers them detached, and this is with regard to contracting ritual impurity, even though they are attached [to the spring]. And now [the Gemara] brings a proof that hashakah [purification through contact with a ritual bath] is not [effective] for consecrated items by Torah law, and similarly, regarding teruma the Sages also instituted a higher standard; and the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] is forced.
